answer: Fingerprints are counted in voyage, thus the distribution is public, and fable lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a lagoon header, so 4207 keys running one model collapse to a single share. A farm of 240 pays that 89 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
